chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Amr ibn Aban, from Abdul-Hamid, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): We have a neighbor who violates all the prohibitions, to the extent that he leaves the prayer out of preference (or negligently). He said: Glory be to Allah, and great is that. Then he said: Shall I not inform you of one who is worse than him? I said: Yes. He said: The one who is inimical to us (the Ahl al-Bayt) is worse than him.

key_terms.النَّاصِبُ: the inimical one (to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Who is worse than a person who neglects prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elevates the status of *Wilayah* (divine authority) above mere ritual observance by comparing a neighbor who neglects prayer to the *Nasib* (one who bears enmity toward the Ahl al-Bayt). This comparison underscores a key Shia theological principle: while neglecting prayer is a major sin, the spiritual danger of enmity toward the Imams is considered more severe, as it represents a rejection of the core of divine guidance. The term *Nasib* specifically refers to those who actively oppose the Ahl al-Bayt, making this a profound lesson on prioritizing relational fidelity to the Prophet's family over isolated acts of worship.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 23. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Yahya al-’Attar from Ahmad b. Muhammad from Ibn Fadhal from Ali b. ’Uqba from ’Amru b. Aban from Abdul-Hameed who said:
“One who is inimical to us is worse than that.”
